text:
Every rhythmic moon that passes I am called,

by God's grave numbers, to give my life

into another life: a mixture dyed blue ink;

the same strange mixture with which it has been kneaded.


And through my flesh, miserable and tired,

filters a warm wind of promised land,

and my dilated nose drinks, sweet aroma,

the exultant forest and the nourished branch.


A deceptive siren song you sing to me,

cunning nature! You attract and enchant me

so as to load me later with some human fruit.


Deceit for deceit: my beauty slips away

from the solemn call; from this living fever,

some sterile and passing love enjoys.

translation.title: Song of the Astute Woman
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's negotiation with fertility, nature, and chosen sterility.
